lines.en: On the topic of “fate,” I’ve been wondering lately if there’s any merit to it. And how much mental wherewithal would be needed to reach down its throat and retake the even vaguer concept of destiny.
I was raised with the notion of winners winning and losers losing wrapped so tightly around my neck that it could be misconstrued as a noose.
And so here I swing and sway, toyed with by the wind in summer’s fall, knowing that what one is raised to think and know is but one more jaded account of a life someone else has lived.
If I am anything, which I often think I’m not, I am me.
And if there’s anything I know about myself, which I often think there’s not, it’s that the only person who can choose what becomes of my life is the one living it (me).
Or at least that’s how I felt before I learned about God.
Now, I fear that this life has never been mine to live at all. And that “fate” is just a fancy word that grown-ups use to describe His plans for us.
But I walk among them now — the ones I so gradually grew to detest. I’ve learned to see the forest for the trees.
And every single one of them is beautiful.
Even those still growing.
: So what’s the plan now, exactly? Did we really only dress up to look hot in front of each other tonight?
: Are you suggesting that we take to the streets to try and seduce people? Or just lure them into potentially believing that we’re still in high school?
: I’m pretty sure only one of us would be able to pull off the high school thing, so I guess the former if those are the only two options.
: I’m just glad my old uniform still fits. It just comes at the expense of not looking as cougar-ish as you guys.
: Yeah, which is crazy when you factor in how you had infinitely more sex than both Maki and me combined in high school.
: True. But if we’re ranking ourselves based on current statistics, Maki’s the sex champion here. She’s probably boned more dudes in one day than either of us have in our lives.
: To be fair, though, it’s not like our numbers in that department are all that impressive. Excluding Maki, obviously.
: Maki, how many guys have you slept with exactly?
: Who cares? All that matters is I am winning.
: With a body like that, it’s kind of hard to lose.
: Yeah. It’s a shame we’re the only ones who get to see it.
: Well, Akira’s around, isn’t he? We could always go rile him up and take bets on which one of us he jerks off to later. That’s what Christmalloween is all about, right?
: Maybe the Malloween part, sure. I don’t know if he’s here yet, though. I went over there earlier to say hi and it was just the two lady-teachers.
: We could take bets on which of them will masturbate to us? Rin’s mom is a hardcore lesbian at the very least.
: Is she? I thought she was bi?
: She’d be forced to choose a side if we swarmed her. And we all know which side it would be with your teenage appeal, Maki’s goddess body, and my...intellect.
: Is that what the kids are calling boobs these days?
: Kids are doing all sorts of stuff nowadays that never would have worked when we were younger.
: Like what? They don’t seem that different to me. Like...we’re not that old.
: Sure. But Christmalloween costumes in general are way more revealing now than they were back when we were in school. Isn’t that kind of dangerous?
: I feel like at least a quarter of those costumes were purchased directly from your store.
: Why’s it dangerous? Aren’t you the one who’s always preaching about sexual positivity and whatnot? Let the girls have their fun.
: I’m just saying there needs to be a line somewhere, right? Like, if Makoto went out wearing the same outfit I am, I can’t say I’d be happy about it.
: If Makoto went out wearing the same outfit you are, it’d probably just fall off. You’re kind of leagues ahead of her in the proportions department.
: I think I get what Maki’s saying. I’m not really sure if I agree with it, though.
: Yeah, easy for you to say when you literally never have to worry about it. We’ve all seen your daughter’s costumes.
: What’s this about my costumes?
: See?! You literally couldn’t get further away from revealing if you tried!
: What are you talking about?! You can see her entire arms! At least up until the point where they become steel claws.
: Makoto told me that Chika girl’s costume a few years ago was literally just bandages. We can at least agree that is excessive, right?
: I think that entirely depends on the amount of bandages. I still don’t really think it’s a problem, though. They’re just costumes, Maki.
: Oh...I think I understand what this conversation is about now...
: Sana, how do you feel about the revealing nature of some of your friends’ costumes? What’s the teenage perspective on this? Maybe we’re just old.
: To be honest...I feel like most of them only dress that way to try and get Sensei’s attention...
: See, that. That’s weird. He’s an adult. It’s one thing to have a crush on him, but taking their clothes off to try and appeal to him is a completely different story.
: They don’t know what he’s been through. And forcing him into a situation where he suddenly needs to fend off a swarm of half-naked teenagers has gotta be overwhelming for the poor guy.
: But if they like being looked at that way...why is it a problem, exactly?...
: I think Maki’s saying it’s more of a problem because of the situation it puts Sensei in.
: Well...no. I think. Maybe? Blaming the girls for turning on a grown man sounds like it could get me cancelled.
: I just think that maybe we should be a little less lenient when it comes to what we let our children wear for Christmalloween. That’s all.
: Like, Makoto’s costumes are never that risque but she’s still cute.
: Right! Same as Sana.
: Sana’s costumes are definitely something, alright. I’m not sure if “cute” is the word I’d use to describe them, though.
: It’s just one day out of the year, Maki. I think it’s a good thing that we give the girls this much freedom.
: Okay. Well, A — you don’t have a kid and don’t have to worry about this. And B — it’s not just one day. Teenagers are dressing more provactively all the time now.
: Even their uniforms are getting kind of skimpy compared to what we wore. Are you saying you’re just totally cool with that too?
: I mean...yeah. Times change. And I kind of figured you’d be on the side of giving girls the freedom to dress how they want since you have no qualms with literally letting them sell porn.
: In a controlled environment where I know I can keep them safe and educate them, sure! That’s way different than Makoto flashing her panties to some old guy at a train station.
: Sana, cover your ears. I did that once.
: You...didn’t give me enough time to cover my ears...
: You’re indifferent to all of this too then? Even as a mother?
: You’re not afraid of Sana getting lured into the same situation you had to go through because she caught the eye of some predator?
: Should I...leave the room for this?...
: No, you can stay. You’re mature enough to hear this. Just like Makoto’s mature enough to sell dildos and fleshlights and pursue whoever she wants regardless of their age.
: That’s crazy! She’s still in high school!
: High schoolers just aren’t the same anymore, Maki. I deal with them every single day.
: Like, you’d be shocked to hear how sexually active some of these girls are. It’s like there are Saras all over the place now.
: It’s different when it’s with each other than it is with people our age. Like, surely you wouldn’t hook up with a teenager if one started putting the moves on you, right?
: Of course not. But we shouldn’t be punishing teenagers over the actions of the small minority of adults who would. Right, Sara?
: Uhh...yeah? Maybe? Like...you can’t punish someone before they do anything wrong.
: This is protection we’re talking about. Not punishment.
: I’m fine with girls expressing themselves however they want until they start going around and trying to bait older guys into having sex with them. That, I feel the need to step in for.
: If I said I would, then what?
: Then I’d say you’re a disgusting piece of shit who shouldn’t be allowed in public. That’s what.
: Woah. Isn’t that a little excessive, Maki? Haruka’s trying to be civil about this.
: Civil? About having sex with high schoolers? Sorry Sara, but I’m not going to be civil about this. You guys aren’t going to make me feel like the weird one here.
: So yeah. If you went out and fucked some innocent student just because their hormones compelled them to do something stupid, you sure as hell wouldn’t be my friend anymore.
: Hope that answers your question.
: Yeah...I really feel like I shouldn’t have been here for this...
: No, no. You’re fine, baby. Just maybe don’t tell Makoto her mom is in here freaking out over the current state of Christmalloween costumes among teens.
: I just...want what’s best for my daughter. That’s all. So I’m sorry if not wanting her sexualized in front of adults is a little conservative for you guys.
: If it makes you happy...Makoto would probably agree...I don’t think she’s a fan of the...um...more revealing costumes either...
: Thanks, Sana. I needed that.
: Well, don’t get upset! We don’t need to agree on everything to still have a good time. Right, Haruka?
: Uhh...y...yeah...
: Yeah, we can...just not agree on some stuff and...that doesn’t change anything about anyone.
: Until it does.
: And then you hate yourself for never noticing it was coming.
: You know, Rika — I’ve gotta say...I’m proud of these girls. This is probably the least revealing Christmalloween we’ve had yet.
: Yeah...But I still can’t help but feel like there’s someone out there currently talking about how messed up the current state of Christmalloween costumes is as a whole.
: You’re probably only saying that because I keep having to tell you your thong is showing.
: If any of these girls have any intrusive thoughts about the thong of a forty-two year old woman, that’s on them. Not me.
: And also Makoto’s mom since I bought this from her store and I’m pretty sure this dress is one size smaller than it was supposed to be.
: Either that or this is just what happens when you buy your costume from a porn shop.
: What do you know about porn shops? You’re in your mid-twenties. All your kind knows is free porn and getting sex toys delivered right to your front door.
: Don’t say “your kind” to black people. It’s frowned upon.
: Sorry, Imani. But I don’t see color.
: Yeah, don’t say that either. That’s even worse.
: You are literally impossible to please without being a well-endowed man named Akira.
: Oh, he pleases me all right. I just wish his-
: Sorry, hold on a second. Tsuneyo! Get out of here and go back to the party. The bedroom is for the adults.
: Then perhaps that is where the two of you should go, as I am currently standing guard in the hall and can not afford to let conversation distract me from doing my job.
: Girl’s so quiet I straight up forgot she was there.
: Try just covering one of your eyes instead! It works way better! I’ve only bumped into stuff like four times tonight, yet I still maintain the sexual appeal of a somewhat blind woman!
: I am concerned not with sexual appeal for I have already mastered this aspect of being a woman. The time has come for me to focus on defense instead.
: So anyway, what were you saying?
: Why bother stopping the conversation to prevent Tsuneyo from hearing it if you’re just going to start it right back up the second she refuses to leave?
: Oh, that’s easy. I already forgot what we were talking about.
: You were discussing the ease with which my original teacher pleases Miss Imai — indicating that the conversation was likely sexual in nature.
: Couldn’t you have been deaf for Christmalloween instead? This whole blind thing ain’t benefiting nobody.
: You say that now. But once our enemies have been vanquished, you will wish that you had never doubted me.
: Guess we can just talk about something else instead? How about Rin? I never get to talk about Rin.
: You legitimately never shut up about Rin.
: Oh, so we’re talking about Rin now? Awesome! Did you know her grades scored in the top ten of her class last semester?
: Bitch, I gave her those grades.
: Oh.
: Ooooooohhh....
: What do you mean, “Ooooooohhh?” Why “Ooooooohhh?”
: Nothing really. I just didn’t think you were the type of teacher to give someone good grades in exchange for favors from their parents.
: There are easier ways to sleep with me, Imani. Just bring me cookies if you want it that badly.
: This is no better than how the last conversation would have gone before we mutually decided to pull the plug.
: I’m sorry. Someone definitely spiked the pumpkin nog. My inhibitions can not be tamed tonight.
: I can tell by the amount of panty-shots I’ve gotten from just being around you over the last few hours.
: I knew I shouldn’t have worn any. Trust yourself in the future, Rika. Your gut is always right.
: You know, we could get in serious trouble if the school found out about these parties. You sure you’re not a liability?
: Trouble? Why would we get in trouble?
: Well...because being around a bunch of scantily clad teens is scandalous enough as-is. But it takes on a new level once one of the teachers is dressed in similar fashion.
: In my defense, I am not technically a teacher. I’m just an advisor.
: Plus, if Akira can get away with it year after year, I doubt it’s a problem for us.
: It’s weird that he got away with it too. Especially considering how gung-ho the whole damn class is about jumping his bones now.
: If I may interject-
: You may not! Go away!
: I just want to say that, despite how gung-ho we have become about jumping the teacher’s bones, he still treats us with respect and dignity. And for that, we are grateful.
: Oh. Well, that certainly makes me feel a little better about all that stuff he said to me the last time he came over to...play Scrabble.
: I’m bad at Scrabble. I don’t know why, but my natural instinct is to just always try to spell names. And apparently that’s against the rules.
: Not actual Scrabble, Rika.
: Oooooooh.
: You mean Boggle.
: Oooooooh!
: You mean sex!
: Damn it, Rika! For once, just prove me wrong about being a liability!
: We’re all liabilities here! Just look at us! There’s never been a bigger group of walking red-flags! Except for that girl over there. What’s her name again? She seems perfect.
: Stop braggin’ about your damn daughter, yo! That shit got old the second time you did it!
